m:sol: Free to walk around at any hour. In the crowds at Sol and in the metro watch out for pickpockets. On Plaza Mayor from late November to 31 December there's the Christmas market (in 2025 from 27 November to 31 December, 10am–9pm; the 2026 dates will be announced in autumn).
m:palacio: Ticket €18 (plus €0.77 online fee), reduced €9. From October to March open Monday–Saturday 10am–6pm and Sunday and holidays 10am–4pm; the ticket office closes an hour earlier. Closed on 1 and 6 January, 1 May and 25 December; on 24 and 31 December it closes at 3pm. It may close without notice for official ceremonies. EU citizens enter free Monday to Thursday 4–6pm (October–March), but the queue is long. Data from a guide citing the Patrimonio Nacional website, to be confirmed on patrimonionacional.es.
m:almudena: Entry to the cathedral is free (suggested donation €1), every day 10am–8:30pm (until 9pm in July and August), but it can't be visited during services. The museum and dome cost €7 and are only open Monday to Saturday, 10am–2:30pm. Data from a guide, to be confirmed.
m:prado: Ticket €15, reduced €7.50 (over 65); under-18s and students up to 25 go free. Open Monday–Saturday 10am–8pm, Sunday and holidays 10am–7pm. The permanent collection is free Monday–Saturday 6–8pm and Sunday 5–7pm, with a queue. Closed on 1 January, 1 May and 25 December; on 24 and 31 December 10am–2pm. Data from a guide checked against the official website on 13 September 2026: confirm on museodelprado.es.
m:reina: Ticket €12; free for under-18s, over-65s and students. Open Monday and Wednesday–Saturday 10am–9pm, Sunday 10am–2:30pm; closed on Tuesdays. Free entry (with a free ticket booked online) Monday and Wednesday–Saturday 7–9pm and Sunday 12:30–2:30pm. Also closed on 1 and 6 January, 1 and 15 May, 9 November, and 24, 25 and 31 December. Data from a guide checked on 13 September 2026: confirm on museoreinasofia.es.
m:thyssen: Ticket €14, reduced €10. On Mondays (noon–4pm) the permanent collection is free, without a ticket. Tuesday–Friday and Sunday 10am–7pm; Saturday 10am–11pm, with temporary exhibitions free from 9 to 11pm. Closed on 1 January, 1 May and 25 December; on 24 and 31 December 10am–3pm. Data from a guide (14 September 2026), to be confirmed on museothyssen.org.
m:retiro: Open every day from 6am to 10pm from October to March (until midnight from April to September), free entry; in strong wind the city closes it. The Palacio de Cristal is closed for works and covered by the artwork «Fardo» until 1 January 2027. The Palacio de Velázquez, free, is open 10am–6pm from October to March. Rowing boats on the lake €6–8 for up to 4 people, 45 minutes (dated fare, to be confirmed).
m:debod: The outside is free at any hour. The inside (free entry, 30 people at a time, half an hour maximum) is open Tuesday–Sunday and holidays 10am–8pm, last entry 7:30pm, from 16 September to 14 June; closed on Mondays, 1 and 6 January, 1 May, and 24, 25 and 31 December. Booking is free and recommended. Data from a guide (September 2026).
m:granvia: Free to walk around at any hour. In the evening it's nicer with the lights. The Círculo de Bellas Artes (Calle de Alcalá 42) has a paid rooftop terrace: I didn't check the price. There are lots of pickpockets here: backpack in front.
m:letras: Free to stroll around. The terraces on the square cost more than the inner streets; in the evening the neighbourhood is full of bars.
m:sanmiguel: Free entry, you only pay for what you take: about €15–20 per person for two or three tastes and a glass, at tourist-area prices (from a guide). Open Sunday–Thursday 10am–midnight; Friday, Saturday and the eve of holidays 10am–1am. Best between 11am and 1pm or between 4 and 7pm: at weekend lunchtimes and after 9pm it's packed.
vd:sangines: Madrid's most famous chocolatería, in an alley near Sol, open since 1894: hot churros to dip in a cup of thick chocolate. No bookings, you pay for what you order.
vp:sangines: Churros with chocolate about €6–8 per person (price not read, prices are displayed inside). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed: open 24 hours from Thursday to Sunday.
vd:mallorquina: The historic pâtisserie on the Puerta del Sol: napolitanas (pastries) with custard, chocolate or ham and cheese, mille-feuille, croissants and palmeras. Upstairs there's a café overlooking the square.
vp:mallorquina: A napolitana with a coffee is around €4–6 (price not read). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed.
vd:campana: The bar a short walk from Plaza Mayor where you eat the bocadillo de calamares, the fried squid sandwich: Madrid's speciality. Eaten standing at the counter, often with a caña.
vp:campana: The bocadillo costs about €4.50 and it's cash only (guide, September 2026). One guide says it's closed on Mondays, another open every day 10am–11pm: hours to be confirmed.
vd:labra: An 1860 tavern near Sol where the Spanish Socialist Party was founded: come for the tajadas de bacalao, salt cod fried in batter, and the croquetas. Order at the counter and eat standing up.
vp:labra: A tajada de bacalao and a croqueta are a few euros each (prices not read, budget range). Hours from Time Out (2025), to be confirmed: closed on 1 January.
vd:abuelo: A bodega open since 1906 near the Puerta del Sol, famous for gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns) and gambas a la plancha, to go with the house sweet wine.
vp:abuelo: About €16–30 per person (a guide). Hours from esMadrid, to be confirmed.
vd:revuelta: A historic tavern between Plaza Mayor and La Latina: the one dish is fried salt cod (bacalao rebozado), taken at the counter with a caña. Small and always full.
vp:revuelta: Budget range (Time Out: 1 out of 4), about €8–12 for a taste and a beer (estimate, menu not read). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed: closed on Mondays.
vd:brillante: The bar opposite Atocha station, standing or on the terrace: bocadillo de calamares, churros with chocolate at breakfast, patatas bravas and huevos rotos. Open from morning to evening.
vp:brillante: Bocadillo de calamares from €3.50 (mini) to €7 (large); €1.50–2 more on the terrace (Time Out). A September 2026 guide says it's closed on Tuesdays: hours to be confirmed.
vd:alberto: The 1827 tavern in the Barrio de las Letras, with a zinc bar and vermouth on tap: the home of callos a la madrileña (tripe), rabo estofado (oxtail) and albóndigas.
vp:alberto: Mid-range (Time Out: 2 out of 4), about €20–30 for dinner (estimate, menu not read). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed: closed on Mondays; Sunday lunch only.
vd:antonio: An 1830 tavern in Lavapiés, the oldest in Madrid still open: a zinc bar, walls with bulls' heads and traditional cooking like cocido madrileño, tortillita de camarones and torrezno.
vp:antonio: Menú del día for €14 with first course, main, dessert and drink (Time Out). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed: closed on Mondays, Sunday lunch only.
vd:comercial: Madrid's oldest café still open, since 1887: mirrors, the original counter and marble tables. For breakfast, an afternoon snack or a light dinner with croquetas, ensaladilla and patatas bravas.
vp:comercial: Mid-range (Time Out: 2 out of 4), a coffee with a pastry about €6–8 (estimate, menu not read). Hours from Time Out (2019 review): to be confirmed.
vd:ardosa: An old-style Malasaña bodega: the pincho de tortilla runny in the middle, croquetas, callos and vermouth on tap. Packed at vermouth time.
vp:ardosa: Budget range (Time Out: 1 out of 4), a pincho of tortilla and a caña about €5–7 (estimate, menu not read). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed.
vd:sanmiguel: The 1916 covered market turned into a gourmet market: lots of stalls with tapas, jamón, oysters and sweets, to taste standing up. It's pricier and more touristy than neighbourhood bars.
vp:sanmiguel: About €15–20 per person for two or three tastes and a glass (guide, September 2026). Hours from the market website via a guide.
cd:bernabeu: Real Madrid's museum, stands and pitch.
cd:sorolla: The Valencian painter's house and garden, still furnished.
cd:galdiano: A private collection with Goya, El Greco and Bosch, in a mansion.
cd:descalzas: A Renaissance convent with Rubens tapestries and royal treasures.
cd:moncloa: The 92-metre tower with views of the Sierra de Guadarrama.
cd:lasventas: Spain's most important neo-Mudéjar bullring, with a small museum.
cd:arqueologico: From prehistory to the Middle Ages, with the Lady of Elche.
cd:teleferico: The cable car over the Manzanares to the Casa de Campo.
cd:zooaq: Pandas, dolphins and an aquarium, in the Casa de Campo.
cd:caixamadrid: A museum with a Patrick Blanc vertical garden and temporary exhibitions.
